description: We’re five students who enjoy turning curiosity into working solutions. Our skills include AI/ML, programming, data analysis, research, and creative problem-solving. We also love making difficult concepts easier to understand through animations and interactive visuals. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we want to combine our strengths, explore NASA’s data, and build a creative solution that is useful and easy to understand.
summary:
Cosmic Explorer is an interactive, web-based storytelling project that explores the scientific stories behind equipment left on the Moon and Mars. It brings selected spacecraft, landers, rovers, instruments, and mission hardware into one accessible experience, explaining why each was sent, what it was designed to do, what scientists learned from it, and why it remains where its mission ended.

Rather than treating these objects as forgotten machines, Cosmic Explorer presents them as lasting evidence of human exploration, engineering, and discovery. Through visual storytelling and easy-to-understand explanations, the project aims to make planetary science and space exploration more engaging for students and curious visitors. It connects the achievements of past missions with the possibilities of future exploration.
details:
Cosmic Explorer is a browser-based educational experience created to bring the stories of NASA's exploration hardware closer to people. The project focuses on selected equipment left on the Moon and Mars, including spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments.

The website allows visitors to explore these missions through visual storytelling and accessible explanations. Each story connects a piece of hardware to its original purpose, the mission it belonged to, the scientific contribution it made, and what happened after its mission ended.

Our idea was to look beyond the word "discarded." These machines may no longer be active, but their contributions to science and human exploration remain important. We wanted to show that even equipment left behind has a meaningful story.

The project is designed especially for students and people interested in space exploration. We considered factual accuracy, readability, visual presentation, and ease of navigation while developing the experience.

We used Google AI Studio with Gemini-assisted development to help build and refine the website. The project concept, research selection, storytelling direction, and final content curation were shaped by Team Xtream. NASA resources were used to support the mission information and historical context presented in the project.

Our goal is to make space exploration history easier to understand and inspire curiosity about the science and engineering behind future missions.
